doc.title: Johnny Varro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Daughter and advice about a jazz career
summary: His daughter's brief singing career and whether to recommend jazz.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: All right. Well it’s been a really fun conversation. I see your daughter sings is that right?
Well she used to. She doesn’t anymore. She’s out of the business now. But she had a little shot at it and enjoyed it while it lasted. It got a little tough. There’s not that much work around.
Yeah, I was just going to say, like would you recommend a career in jazz to a young person these days?

Why not? I mean if they have the gumption to get into it and stick with it and work it out, and the talent of course, sure why not. But Heidi wasn’t really that hot in it. I don’t know what it was with her.
You have to be kind of driven I think.

Yeah. It’s a rough business, it really is tough. And there’s no point in getting into it if she wasn’t going to give it her whole heart and soul and I don’t think she was ready for that. And she’s got other things going that she’s doing very well at, so I’m happy. As long as she’s happy, that’s the important thing, the main thing.
